task.description: WF-02 Step 5 -- independently re-derive, from shipped code and tests (not from any prior handoff's narrative), whether all seven of REQ-075's acceptance criteria are genuinely met, before REQ-075 is marked done.
acceptance_criteria: each of the 7 ACs independently re-checked against actual code/tests
full test suite independently re-run (not trusted from TEST-RUNNER's report)
an independent mutation test on the authorization mechanism itself, distinct from TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's, given AC2's consequence
PASS only if all 7 ACs are confirmed; FAIL on any doubt regarding AC1/AC2/AC5

result.summary:
Independently re-verified all seven REQ-075 acceptance criteria against actual shipped code (not prior handoff narratives).

AC1 (non-admin GET /tenants -> 403, zero data, full-body): read lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex's with_authorization/4 (evaluate_access/2 called before any Repo call; Deny403 short-circuits) and test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs's 'AC1' describe block -- asserts the exact full problem-detail body plus refute on other.tenant.slug/'items'/'count' substrings. Confirmed met.

AC2 (4 verbs cross-tenant rejection, row unchanged): read all four tests (GET/PATCH/deactivate/reactivate) in the 'AC2' describe block -- each asserts 403 AND Repo.get!/1 row-equality (or status) unchanged. Traced Letflow.Api.Authorization: :TenantsManage is granted only via role_allows?(:PLATFORM_ADMIN, _) -> true; no other role clause lists :TenantsManage (verified full role_allows?/2 body, lines 362-397). Ran my OWN independent mutation test distinct from TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's (which inverted with_authorization/4's Deny/Allow branch handling): I instead injected a role_allows?(_role, :TenantsManage) -> true clause ahead of the real matrix, breaking role-matching itself rather than branch ordering. Result: 7/20 tenants_test.exs tests failed under this mutation (mix test test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs -> 13/20 passed), then reverted (git status --short clean afterward) and reconfirmed 20/20 passed. This is a second, structurally different mechanism than TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-03b mutation, both now independently proving the authorization gate is load-bearing. AC2 confirmed met with high confidence.

AC3 (own-tenant rule, both directions): read the moduledoc's 'Own-tenant rule (AC3)' section -- states no carve-out, ported as-is from R-Co. Read Letflow.Identity.get_tenant_by_slug/1 and patch_tenant/2 -- both Repo.get_by(Tenant, slug: slug) with no actor-identity comparison, so PLATFORM_ADMIN-gating is identical whether or not the target is the caller's own tenant. Read both directions' tests in the 'AC3' describe block: PLATFORM_ADMIN GET/PATCH on own tenant -> 200 (allowed direction), non-PLATFORM_ADMIN GET/PATCH on own tenant -> 403 + row unchanged (denied direction). Trusted the twice-independently-verified R-Co source claim (Step 1/1b) per task guidance and focused on shipped code matching it -- it does. Confirmed met.

AC4 (real migration replay via information_schema, not trusting the 201): read the 'AC4/AC7' test -- switches Sandbox to :auto, POSTs, then independently queries information_schema.tables for table_name='events' in the newly provisioned schema (not merely checking the 201 status). Confirmed met -- not trusting the 201 alone.

AC5 (deactivated tenant, TenantStatus, all methods, 403, PLATFORM_ADMIN-exempt): read lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex's call/2 line-by-line myself -- cond clause 'tenant.status == :inactive and @platform_admin not in roles -> reject_inactive(conn)' runs unconditionally on every method (no method guard on this branch, unlike the :migrating branch which is write-method-gated), checked before the :migrating branch. reject_inactive/1 returns 403 'tenant_inactive'. Read test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs's AC5 describe blocks: GET and POST both -> 403 for non-admin; PLATFORM_ADMIN GET/POST both pass through unchanged; no-roles caller also rejected; :active/:migrating tenants unaffected. This is the piece requiring the out-of-sequence REVIEWER pre-approval (step-01c) -- gave it its own independent read rather than trusting the sign-off summary, and the shipped cond ordering and exemption match exactly what step-01c authorized. Confirmed met.

AC6 (moduledoc risk statement): read the shipped @moduledoc's 'THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK ROUTE GROUP IN S4 (AC6)' section verbatim -- states operation outside REQ-072 prefix-scoping, names PLATFORM_ADMIN as the only protection, and explains why (no second isolation layer, platform-wide vs single-tenant blast radius). Confirmed met.

AC7 (moduledoc REQ-076 relationship): read the shipped @moduledoc's 'Relationship to REQ-076 (AC7)' section verbatim -- states both POST /tenants and REQ-076's onboarding endpoint call the same Letflow.TenantProvisioning primitives, one platform-admin path and one self-service path, neither reimplementing provisioning. Confirmed met.

Independently re-ran the full test suite as a normal blocking foreground call (mix test, no Monitor/background wait): Result: 1542 passed (5 properties, 1537 tests), exit code 0, matching TEST-RUNNER's step-04 aggregate exactly. Also independently reran the four REQ-075-specific test files together (test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs, test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs, test/letflow/identity/tenant_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs): 74/74 passed, 0 failures.

Verdict: PASS. All seven acceptance criteria independently confirmed met from actual shipped code and tests, not from any prior handoff's narrative. No doubt on AC1, AC2, or AC5.
